definition: Margin-infused relaxed algorithm (MIRA) is a machine learning and online algorithm for multiclass classification problems.
details: It is designed to learn a set of parameters (vector or matrix) by processing all the given training examples one-by-one and updating the parameters according to each training example, so that the current training example is classified correctly with a margin against incorrect classifications at least as large as their loss. The change of the parameters is kept as small as possible. A two-class version called binary MIRA simplifies the algorithm by not requiring the solution of a quadratic programming problem (see below). When used in a one-vs-all configuration, binary MIRA can be extended to a multiclass learner that approximates full MIRA, but may be faster to train. explainer.lead: MIRA is an online algorithm for multiclass classification that updates its parameters one training example at a time. It matters because it combines large-margin learning with minimal, loss-aware updates, making it practical for tasks that arrive as a stream.

tiers.eli5: Imagine adjusting your guesses after each answer sheet you see, but changing them as little as possible—just enough to get that one right with a comfortable buffer.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for online multiclass tasks where data arrives sequentially and parameters must be updated incrementally. A common pitfall is the cost of solving the underlying quadratic program at each step unless a simplified variant is used.
tiers.paperLevel: For each training example, parameters are updated so the correct class is classified with a margin at least as large as the loss against incorrect classifications, while the parameter change is kept as small as possible. The two-class version, binary MIRA, avoids solving a quadratic program; the full multiclass form requires one per update.

explainer.example: A spam-style multiclass tagger processes one labelled message at a time and nudges its weight matrix just enough to separate the correct tag from the wrong ones by at least their loss.
